gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with excuses; deliver on time or do not bother coming.
gaps.explanation: 'Has no patience with' — 'no' directly negates the noun.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: We went to the exhibition, but there was ___ worth seeing.
gaps.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast, so 'nothing worth seeing' fits the disappointment.

gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ came to the afternoon lecture.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly anyone' is already negative — do not add 'no one'.

gaps.sentence: ___ money was spent on advertising last year.
___ everyone in the office passed the safety test.
gaps.hint: the only adverb that can modify 'everyone'
gaps.explanation: 'Almost everyone' is the standard pattern; 'each', 'all' and 'every' cannot directly precede 'everyone'.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ of room for improvement in this essay.
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of room' is the fixed pattern; 'a lot of' would need the article 'a', which is not in the sentence.
